I think there is a serious bug in the system regarding the editing and saving of regular markdown files.

I opened the markdown file through the link on a conversation on an action popup. then changed some things to the file. I think i clicked on it again from within the action popup, closed it, opened some other markdown files, including the card that triggered the generation of the markdown file I edited.

In the ui everything looked ok, but the agent reported it could no longer find the file.

I closed and reopened the project and now the file was gone, but we had 2 duplicates of the card file. so something went seriously wrong her. perhaps in the save or commit process of the markdown editor in listview

design/architecture\data_saving_and_commits.md:32:A commit-only path (`CommitRequest.paths`) is a repository path the batch stages and commits as it exists on disk at flush time; the renderer writes no content and registers no persistence outcome. import { CAN_REDO_COMMAND, CAN_UNDO_COMMAND, type LexicalEditor } from 'lexical'
import type { OpenDocument } from '../../../services/open_files_service'

const HISTORY_MERGE_DELAY_MS = 1000
const CARD_SECTION_KEY = 'body'
const PROMPT_SECTION_KEY = 'prompt'

interface MarkdownDocumentHistory {
    historyState: HistoryState

function sectionKey(target: MarkdownDocumentTarget) {
    if (!target.section) return CARD_SECTION_KEY
    return target.section.kind === 'prompt' ? PROMPT_SECTION_KEY : `phrase:${target.section.identity}`
}

function copyHistoryState(target: HistoryState, source: HistoryState) {
    target.current = source.current
    target.redoStack = source.redoStack
    target.undoStack = source.undoStack
}

function rebindHistoryState(historyState: HistoryState, editor: LexicalEditor) {
    if (historyState.current) historyState.current.editor = editor
    for (const entry of historyState.redoStack) entry.editor = editor
    for (const entry of historyState.undoStack) entry.editor = editor
}

function ensureCurrentEditorState(historyState: HistoryState, editor: LexicalEditor) {
    if (!historyState.current) historyState.current = { editor, editorState: editor.getEditorState() }
}

/** Owns binding-local Lexical histories keyed by canonical document and section. */

    readonly sharedHistoryState = createEmptyHistoryState()

    private editor: LexicalEditor | null = null
    private pendingTarget: MarkdownDocumentTarget | null = null

    get canRedo() { return this.sharedHistoryState.redoStack.length > 0 }
    get canUndo() { return this.sharedHistoryState.undoStack.length > 0 }

    attachEditor(editor: LexicalEditor, target: MarkdownDocumentTarget | null, markdown: string) {
        this.persistActiveDocument()
        this.editor = editor
        for (const sections of this.documents.values()) {
            for (const { historyState } of sections.values()) rebindHistoryState(historyState, editor)
        }
        if (!target) {

        copyHistoryState(this.sharedHistoryState, document.historyState)
        ensureCurrentEditorState(document.historyState, editor)
        copyHistoryState(this.sharedHistoryState, document.historyState)
        this.activeTarget = target
        this.pendingTarget = null
    }

    detachEditor(editor: LexicalEditor) {
        if (this.editor === editor) this.editor = null
    }

    syncToolbarAvailability(editor: LexicalEditor) {
        editor.dispatchCommand(CAN_UNDO_COMMAND, this.canUndo)
        editor.dispatchCommand(CAN_REDO_COMMAND, this.canRedo)

        const unregister = registerHistory(editor, this.sharedHistoryState, HISTORY_MERGE_DELAY_MS)

The likely cause is a document-switch race in the shared list editor:

- Cards and regular Markdown reuse one long-lived editor.
- During switching, `activeTargetRef` changes before the editor replacement has fully settled. [markdown_editor.tsx](C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/editor/markdown_editor.tsx:218)

Flush the outgoing document, ignore editor callbacks during programmatic replacement, and activate the new target only after its expected Markdown becomes the editor baseline. I think there is a serious bug in the system regarding the editing and saving of regular markdown files.

I opened the markdown file through the link on a conversation on an action popup. then changed some things to the file. I think i clicked on it again from within the action popup, closed it, opened some other markdown files, including the card that triggered the generation of the markdown file I edited.

In the ui everything looked ok, but the agent reported it could no longer find the file.

I closed and reopened the project and now the file was gone, but we had 2 duplicates of the card file. so something went seriously wrong her. perhaps in the save or commit process of the markdown editor in listview

## Current state

Regular Markdown files and cards use the same lifetime-stable `CardEditor`. The editor stores the active target separately from the Markdown editor instance. During a document switch, it flushes the outgoing content, changes the active target, and then replaces the editor content.

The programmatic replacement can still produce editor change callbacks after the active target changed. `handleEditorChange` applies every callback to the current target, not the target that initiated the change. Rapid reopen, close, and document switches can therefore apply one document's content to another document. The normal save pipeline then persists the corrupted in-memory document at its target path.

Existing tests cover ordinary switching and saving, but not delayed rich-editor callbacks across the reported open-edit-reopen-close-switch sequence.

## implementation details

* Make a list-editor document switch one transaction. Flush the outgoing target before starting the replacement and do not activate the incoming target until its expected Markdown is established as the editor baseline.
